     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.ChiFiniteness
     7	import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.MulEquiv
     8	
     9	/-!
    10	# The χ-ledger: `chi_step`, `chi_divisorSheaf`, and Riemann–Roch-lite
    11	
    12	The Euler-characteristic ledger for divisor sheaves on the curve bundle `X` (integral,
    13	smooth of relative dimension one and quasi-compact over a field `K`, with finite `H⁰` and
    14	`H¹` of the structure sheaf — the two instance hypotheses through which properness enters):
    15	
    16	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chi_skyModule`: `χ(sky_x M) = dim_K M` — the skyscraper contribution.
    17	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chi_step` (★ ledger keystone): the one-point dévissage step
    18	  `χ(𝒪(D)) = χ(𝒪(D − x)) + [κ(x) : K]`, from the additivity of `χ` along the dévissage
    19	  short exact sequence `0 → 𝒪(D − x) → 𝒪(D) → sky_x J → 0` and `dim_K J = residueDeg x`.
    20	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chi_divisorSheaf` (★ ledger keystone): the closed ledger
    21	  `χ(𝒪(D)) = χ(𝒪_X) + deg D`, by dévissage induction from `𝒪(0) ≅ 𝒪_X`.
    22	* `AlgebraicGeometry.deg_divOf`: principal divisors have degree zero — transport `χ`
    23	  along the multiplication isomorphism `𝒪(0) ≅ 𝒪(0 − div g)` and cancel in the ledger.
    24	* `AlgebraicGeometry.riemann_inequality` (G9): `deg D + χ(𝒪_X) ≤ h⁰(𝒪(D))`.
    25	* `AlgebraicGeometry.h0_nsmul_point_unbounded` (G9): `h⁰(𝒪(n·x))` is unbounded in `n`,
    26	  for any closed point `x` — no rational point is needed, only `residueDeg x ≥ 1`.
    27	
    28	All statements are phrased against the one-point divisor `CurveDivisor.single hx 1`
    29	(definitionally the dévissage twist: `devissageDivisor_eq_sub`).
    30	-/
    31	
    32	set_option autoImplicit false
    33	
    34	universe u
    35	
    36	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite TopologicalSpace
    37	
    38	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    39	
    40	open Scheme
    41	
    42	/-! ## The skyscraper contribution -/
    43	
    44	section Skyscraper
    45	
    46	variable {K : Type u} [CommRing K] {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
    47	
    48	/-- `h⁰` of a skyscraper sheaf is the dimension of its value module. -/
    49	theorem h0_skyModule (x : X) (M : ModuleCat.{u} K) :
    50	    Sheaf.h0 (skyModule x M) = Module.finrank K M :=
    51	  (skyModuleGammaEquiv x M).finrank_eq
    52	
    53	/-- **The Euler characteristic of a skyscraper** is the dimension of its value module:
    54	`h¹` vanishes and `h⁰` is computed by `skyModuleGammaEquiv`. -/
    55	theorem chi_skyModule [Nontrivial K] (x : X) (M : ModuleCat.{u} K) :
    56	    Sheaf.chi (skyModule x M) = Module.finrank K M := by
    57	  rw [Sheaf.chi_eq_h0 (skyModule_subsingleton_hModule_one x M), h0_skyModule]
    58	
    59	end Skyscraper
    60	
    61	/-! ## The ledger -/
    62	
    63	section Ledger
    64	
    65	variable (K : Type u) [Field K] {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
    66	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))] [IsIntegral X]
    67	  [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
    68	  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf K) 0)]
    69	  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf K) 1)]
    70	
    71	/-- **The dévissage step of the χ-ledger** (★): subtracting a closed point `x` from the
    72	divisor drops the Euler characteristic by the residue degree `[κ(x) : K]`:
    73	`χ(𝒪(D)) = χ(𝒪(D − x)) + residueDeg x`. The divisor `D − CurveDivisor.single hx 1` is
    74	definitionally the dévissage twist `devissageDivisor hx D` of the landed short exact
    75	sequence (`devissageDivisor_eq_sub`). -/
    76	theorem chi_step {x : X} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint X) (D : X.CurveDivisor) :
    77	    Sheaf.chi (X.divisorSheaf K D) =
    78	      Sheaf.chi (X.divisorSheaf K (D - CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) + X.residueDeg K x := by
    79	  have hS := devissageSES_shortExact K hx D
    80	  -- the five finiteness inputs and the `H¹(sky) = 0` input, in the `devissageSES` spelling
    81	  haveI h₁0 : Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (devissageSES K hx D).X₁ 0) :=
    82	    moduleFinite_hModule_divisorSheaf_zero K (devissageDivisor hx D)
    83	  haveI h₁1 : Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (devissageSES K hx D).X₁ 1) :=
    84	    moduleFinite_hModule_divisorSheaf_one K (devissageDivisor hx D)
    85	  haveI h₂0 : Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (devissageSES K hx D).X₂ 0) :=
    86	    moduleFinite_hModule_divisorSheaf_zero K D
    87	  haveI h₂1 : Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (devissageSES K hx D).X₂ 1) :=
    88	    moduleFinite_hModule_divisorSheaf_one K D
    89	  haveI h₃0 : Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (devissageSES K hx D).X₃ 0) :=
    90	    haveI := moduleFinite_jumpModule K hx D
    91	    moduleFinite_hModule_skyModule_zero x (jumpModule K hx D)
    92	  haveI h₃1 : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (devissageSES K hx D).X₃ 1) :=
    93	    skyModule_subsingleton_hModule_one x (jumpModule K hx D)
    94	  have hadd := Sheaf.chi_eq_add_of_shortExact hS
    95	  -- identify the three χ's with their divisor-sheaf/skyscraper spellings (definitional)
    96	  have hX₂ : Sheaf.chi (devissageSES K hx D).X₂ = Sheaf.chi (X.divisorSheaf K D) := rfl
    97	  have hX₁ : Sheaf.chi (devissageSES K hx D).X₁ =
    98	      Sheaf.chi (X.divisorSheaf K (D - CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) := rfl
    99	  have hX₃ : Sheaf.chi (devissageSES K hx D).X₃ = (X.residueDeg K x : ℤ) := by
   100	    have h := chi_skyModule x (jumpModule K hx D)
   101	    rw [finrank_jumpModule K hx D] at h
   102	    exact h
   103	  rw [hX₂, hX₁, hX₃] at hadd
   104	  exact hadd
   105	
   106	/-- **The χ-ledger, closed** (★): for every Weil divisor `D` on the curve bundle,
   107	`χ(𝒪(D)) = χ(𝒪_X) + deg D`. Base case `𝒪(0) ≅ 𝒪_X`, step `chi_step`, glue
   108	`CurveDivisor.induction_devissage`. -/
   109	theorem chi_divisorSheaf (D : X.CurveDivisor) :
   110	    Sheaf.chi (X.divisorSheaf K D) =
   111	      Sheaf.chi (X.moduleKSheaf K) + CurveDivisor.deg K D := by
   112	  refine Scheme.CurveDivisor.induction_devissage
   113	    (P := fun D => Sheaf.chi (X.divisorSheaf K D) =
   114	      Sheaf.chi (X.moduleKSheaf K) + CurveDivisor.deg K D)
   115	    ?_ (fun {x} hx D => ?_) D
   116	  · rw [Sheaf.chi_congr (divisorSheafZeroIso K), CurveDivisor.deg_zero, add_zero]
   117	  · rw [devissageDivisor_eq_sub hx D]
   118	    have hstep := chi_step K hx D
   119	    have hdeg := deg_devissageDivisor K hx D
   120	    rw [devissageDivisor_eq_sub hx D] at hdeg
   121	    constructor <;> intro h <;> omega
   122	
   123	/-- **Principal divisors have degree zero**: `deg (div g) = 0` for a unit `g` of the
   124	function field. Multiplication by `g` identifies `𝒪(0)` with `𝒪(0 − div g)`
   125	(`mulEquivDivisorSheaf`), so the two sides of the χ-ledger force the degrees to agree. -/
   126	theorem deg_divOf (g : X.functionFieldˣ) :
   127	    CurveDivisor.deg K (Scheme.divOf (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) g) = 0 := by
   128	  have hcongr := Sheaf.chi_congr (mulEquivDivisorSheaf K g (0 : X.CurveDivisor))
   129	  rw [chi_divisorSheaf K (0 : X.CurveDivisor),
   130	    chi_divisorSheaf K ((0 : X.CurveDivisor) - Scheme.divOf (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) g),
   131	    CurveDivisor.deg_zero, zero_sub, CurveDivisor.deg_neg] at hcongr
   132	  omega
   133	
   134	/-- **The Riemann inequality** (G9, general conditional form): for every Weil divisor `D`,
   135	`deg D + χ(𝒪_X) ≤ h⁰(𝒪(D))` — from the χ-ledger and `h¹ ≥ 0`. The curve-level
   136	`deg D + 1 − genus` form is derived in `ChiCurve`. -/
   137	theorem riemann_inequality (D : X.CurveDivisor) :
   138	    CurveDivisor.deg K D + Sheaf.chi (X.moduleKSheaf K) ≤
   139	      (Sheaf.h0 (X.divisorSheaf K D) : ℤ) := by
   140	  have h := chi_divisorSheaf K D
   141	  have hchi : Sheaf.chi (X.divisorSheaf K D) ≤ (Sheaf.h0 (X.divisorSheaf K D) : ℤ) := by
   142	    rw [Sheaf.chi]
   143	    omega
   144	  omega
   145	
   146	/-- **Unbounded growth of `h⁰` along multiples of a point** (G9): for every closed point
   147	`x` and every bound `N` there is `n` with `N ≤ h⁰(𝒪(n · x))`. No rational point is
   148	needed: `residueDeg x ≥ 1` suffices. -/
   149	theorem h0_nsmul_point_unbounded {x : X} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint X) (N : ℕ) :
   150	    ∃ n : ℕ, N ≤ Sheaf.h0 (X.divisorSheaf K (n • CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) := by
   151	  have key : ∀ n : ℕ, (n : ℤ) - Sheaf.h1 (X.moduleKSheaf K) ≤
   152	      (Sheaf.h0 (X.divisorSheaf K (n • CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) : ℤ) := by
   153	    intro n
   154	    have hchi := chi_divisorSheaf K (n • CurveDivisor.single hx 1)
   155	    rw [Scheme.CurveDivisor.nsmul_single_one hx n,
   156	      Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg_single' K hx (n : ℤ)] at hchi
   157	    have hchile : Sheaf.chi (X.divisorSheaf K (n • CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) ≤
   158	        (Sheaf.h0 (X.divisorSheaf K (n • CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) : ℤ) := by
   159	      rw [Sheaf.chi]
   160	      omega
   161	    have hres : (1 : ℤ) ≤ (X.residueDeg K x : ℤ) := by
   162	      exact_mod_cast Scheme.residueDeg_pos hx
   163	    have hmul : (n : ℤ) * 1 ≤ (n : ℤ) * (X.residueDeg K x : ℤ) :=
   164	      mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hres (by positivity)
   165	    have hchiO : Sheaf.chi (X.moduleKSheaf K) =
   166	        (Sheaf.h0 (X.moduleKSheaf K) : ℤ) - Sheaf.h1 (X.moduleKSheaf K) := rfl
   167	    -- `hchi` rewrote the divisor to `single hx n`; transport back is definitional
   168	    have hchi' : Sheaf.chi (X.divisorSheaf K (n • CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) =
   169	        Sheaf.chi (X.moduleKSheaf K) + (n : ℤ) * (X.residueDeg K x : ℤ) := by
   170	      rw [Scheme.CurveDivisor.nsmul_single_one hx n]
   171	      exact hchi
   172	    omega
   173	  refine ⟨N + Sheaf.h1 (X.moduleKSheaf K), ?_⟩
   174	  have h := key (N + Sheaf.h1 (X.moduleKSheaf K))
   175	  omega
   176	
   177	end Ledger

   179	end AlgebraicGeometry

     8	/-!
     9	# `ModuleCat k`-valued sheaf cohomology and the structure sheaf as a sheaf of modules
    10	
    11	This file provides the cohomology carrier for the genus lane of the Jacobian challenge:
    12	
    13	1. For a small site `(C, J)` and a commutative ring `R`, the degree-`n` cohomology
    14	   `Sheaf.HModule F n` of a sheaf `F` of `R`-modules, defined as the `Ext`-group from the
    15	   constant sheaf with value `R` to `F` (mirroring `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.H`, which is
    16	   `AddCommGrpCat`-valued; ours is `ModuleCat R`-valued so that `Module.finrank` applies).
    17	   Each `Sheaf.HModule F n` is an `R`-module via the `R`-linear structure of the sheaf
    18	   category, and `Sheaf.HModule.map` gives `R`-linear functoriality in `F`.
    19	2. The degree-zero identification `Sheaf.HModule.linearEquiv₀ : HModule F 0 ≃ₗ[R] F(⊤)`
    20	   via `Ext⁰ ≅ Hom` and the constant-sheaf adjunction, together with its naturality.
    21	3. For a scheme `X` over `Spec k`, the structure sheaf of `X` as a sheaf of `k`-modules
    22	   `Scheme.moduleKSheaf` on the small Zariski site `Opens.grothendieckTopology X`, by
    23	   restriction of scalars along the structure morphism, with definitional (`rfl`) access
    24	   to its sections and restriction maps.
    25	
    26	## Universe discipline
    27	
    28	Everything is single-universe: `k : Type u`, `X : Scheme.{u}`, the site `Opens X : Type u`
    29	with hom-types in `Type u`, and coefficients `ModuleCat.{u} k`. Then
    30	`Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) (ModuleCat.{u} k)` is Grothendieck abelian relative
    31	to `u` (`ModuleCat.{u} k` is, and the site is small), hence `HasExt.{u}` holds and
    32	`Sheaf.HModule F n : Type u` with a `Module k` structure — no universe bump anywhere, so
    33	`Module.finrank k` applies directly downstream.
    34	
    35	## Design notes
    36	
    37	* `Sheaf.HModule` is an `abbrev` for `Abelian.Ext`, so the entire mathlib `Ext` API
    38	  (long exact sequences `Ext.covariant_sequence_exact₁/₂/₃`, `Ext.extClass`, the
    39	  Mayer–Vietoris machinery of `CategoryTheory/Sites/SheafCohomology`) applies
    40	  transparently; we do not rebuild any of it.
    41	* No global `Algebra k Γ(X, U)` instance is introduced (it would overlap with mathlib's
    42	  `Algebra R Γ(Spec R, U)` instance via the tautological `OverClass X X`); the module
    43	  structure is carried by the explicit defs `Scheme.overAlgebraMap`/`Scheme.overModule`
    44	  and, where needed, `attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule`.
    45	-/

    47	set_option autoImplicit false

    49	universe u

    51	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite TopologicalSpace
    52	
    53	namespace CategoryTheory
    54	
    55	namespace Sheaf
    56	
    57	variable {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C]
    58	
    59	section HModule
    60	
    61	variable (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (R : Type u) [CommRing R]
    62	  [HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u} R)]
    63	
    64	/-- The constant sheaf of `R`-modules with value `R` on the site `(C, J)`; sheaf cohomology
    65	of sheaves of `R`-modules is `Ext` out of this object. -/
    66	noncomputable def constModuleSheaf : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} R) :=
    67	  (constantSheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} R)).obj (ModuleCat.of R R)
    68	
    69	variable {J R}
    70	
    71	/-- The degree-`n` cohomology of a sheaf of `R`-modules on a small site, as an `Ext`-group
    72	in the Grothendieck abelian category `Sheaf J (ModuleCat R)`. It is a `Type u` carrying a
    73	`Module R` instance (via the `R`-linear structure of the sheaf category). -/
    74	noncomputable abbrev HModule (F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} R)) (n : ℕ) : Type u :=
    75	  Abelian.Ext (constModuleSheaf J R) F n
    76	
    77	namespace HModule
    78	
    79	variable {F G G' : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} R)}
    80	
    81	/-- Functoriality of `Sheaf.HModule` in the sheaf, as an `R`-linear map. -/
    82	noncomputable def map (f : F ⟶ G) (n : ℕ) : HModule F n →ₗ[R] HModule G n :=
    83	  (Abelian.Ext.mk₀ f).postcompOfLinear R (constModuleSheaf J R) (add_zero n)
    84	
    85	lemma map_apply (f : F ⟶ G) {n : ℕ} (x : HModule F n) :
    86	    map f n x = x.comp (Abelian.Ext.mk₀ f) (add_zero n) := rfl
    87	
    88	@[simp]
    89	lemma map_id_apply {n : ℕ} (x : HModule F n) : map (𝟙 F) n x = x := by
    90	  simp [map_apply]
    91	
    92	lemma map_comp_apply (f : F ⟶ G) (g : G ⟶ G') {n : ℕ} (x : HModule F n) :
    93	    map (f ≫ g) n x = map g n (map f n x) := by
    94	  simp [map_apply]
    95	
    96	instance [Injective F] (n : ℕ) : Subsingleton (HModule F (n + 1)) :=
    97	  subsingleton_of_forall_eq 0 fun x ↦ x.eq_zero_of_injective
    98	
    99	end HModule
   100	
   101	section LinearEquivZero
   102	
   103	variable {T : C} (hT : IsTerminal T)
   104	
   105	/-- The hom-equivalence of the constant-sheaf ⊣ global-sections adjunction, upgraded to an
   106	`R`-linear equivalence. -/
   107	noncomputable def constantSheafAdjHomLinearEquiv (M : ModuleCat.{u} R)
   108	    (F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} R)) :
   109	    ((constantSheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} R)).obj M ⟶ F) ≃ₗ[R] (M ⟶ F.obj.obj (op T)) := by
   110	  refine
   111	    { toFun := (constantSheafAdj J (ModuleCat.{u} R) hT).homEquiv M F
   112	      invFun := ((constantSheafAdj J (ModuleCat.{u} R) hT).homEquiv M F).symm
   113	      left_inv := ((constantSheafAdj J (ModuleCat.{u} R) hT).homEquiv M F).left_inv
   114	      right_inv := ((constantSheafAdj J (ModuleCat.{u} R) hT).homEquiv M F).right_inv
   115	      map_add' := fun f g ↦ ?_
   116	      map_smul' := fun r f ↦ ?_ } <;>
   117	  · simp only [Adjunction.homEquiv_apply]
   118	    ext v
   119	    rfl
   120	
   121	lemma constantSheafAdjHomLinearEquiv_apply (M : ModuleCat.{u} R)
   122	    {F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} R)} (φ : (constantSheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} R)).obj M ⟶ F) :
   123	    constantSheafAdjHomLinearEquiv hT M F φ =
   124	      (constantSheafAdj J (ModuleCat.{u} R) hT).homEquiv M F φ := rfl
   125	
   126	lemma constantSheafAdjHomLinearEquiv_naturality (M : ModuleCat.{u} R)
   127	    {F G : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} R)}
   128	    (φ : (constantSheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} R)).obj M ⟶ F) (f : F ⟶ G) :
   129	    constantSheafAdjHomLinearEquiv hT M G (φ ≫ f) =
   130	      constantSheafAdjHomLinearEquiv hT M F φ ≫ f.hom.app (op T) := by
   131	  simp only [constantSheafAdjHomLinearEquiv_apply]
   132	  exact (constantSheafAdj J (ModuleCat.{u} R) hT).homEquiv_naturality_right φ f
   133	
   134	variable (J) in
   135	/-- Morphisms out of the constant sheaf `R` compute global sections, `R`-linearly:
   136	`Hom(R_X, F) ≃ₗ[R] F(⊤)`. -/
   137	noncomputable def constModuleSheafHomEquiv (F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} R)) :
   138	    (constModuleSheaf J R ⟶ F) ≃ₗ[R] F.obj.obj (op T) :=
   139	  (constantSheafAdjHomLinearEquiv hT (ModuleCat.of R R) F).trans
   140	    (ModuleCat.homLinearEquiv.trans (LinearMap.ringLmapEquivSelf R R _))
   141	
   142	lemma constModuleSheafHomEquiv_naturality {F G : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} R)}
   143	    (φ : constModuleSheaf J R ⟶ F) (f : F ⟶ G) :
   144	    constModuleSheafHomEquiv J hT G (φ ≫ f) =
   145	      f.hom.app (op T) (constModuleSheafHomEquiv J hT F φ) := by
   146	  simp only [constModuleSheafHomEquiv]
   147	  rfl
   148	
   149	variable (J) in
   150	/-- Degree-zero cohomology of a sheaf of `R`-modules is its module of global sections
   151	(sections over a terminal object of the site), `R`-linearly. -/
   152	noncomputable def HModule.linearEquiv₀ (F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} R)) :
   153	    HModule F 0 ≃ₗ[R] F.obj.obj (op T) :=
   154	  (Abelian.Ext.linearEquiv₀ (R := R)).trans (constModuleSheafHomEquiv J hT F)
   155	
   156	variable {F G : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} R)} (f : F ⟶ G)
   157	
   158	lemma HModule.linearEquiv₀_map (x : HModule F 0) :
   159	    Abelian.Ext.linearEquiv₀ (R := R) (HModule.map f 0 x) =
   160	      Abelian.Ext.linearEquiv₀ (R := R) x ≫ f := by
   161	  apply (Abelian.Ext.mk₀_bijective (constModuleSheaf J R) G).injective
   162	  simp only [Abelian.Ext.mk₀_linearEquiv₀_apply, ← Abelian.Ext.mk₀_comp_mk₀,
   163	    Abelian.Ext.mk₀_linearEquiv₀_apply]
   164	  exact HModule.map_apply f x
   165	
   166	/-- Naturality of the degree-zero identification. -/
   167	theorem HModule.linearEquiv₀_naturality (x : HModule F 0) :
   168	    f.hom.app (op T) (HModule.linearEquiv₀ J hT F x) =
   169	      HModule.linearEquiv₀ J hT G (HModule.map f 0 x) := by
   170	  simp only [linearEquiv₀, LinearEquiv.trans_apply, HModule.linearEquiv₀_map f x]
   171	  exact (constModuleSheafHomEquiv_naturality hT (Abelian.Ext.linearEquiv₀ x) f).symm
   172	
   173	theorem HModule.linearEquiv₀_symm_naturality (s : F.obj.obj (op T)) :
   174	    HModule.map f 0 ((HModule.linearEquiv₀ J hT F).symm s) =
   175	      (HModule.linearEquiv₀ J hT G).symm (f.hom.app (op T) s) := by
   176	  apply (HModule.linearEquiv₀ J hT G).injective
   177	  simp [← HModule.linearEquiv₀_naturality]
   178	
   179	end LinearEquivZero
   180	
   181	end HModule
   182	
   183	end Sheaf
   184	
   185	end CategoryTheory
   186	
   187	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
   188	
   189	variable (k : Type u) [CommRing k] (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of k))]
   190	
   191	/-- The structure morphism of a scheme over `Spec k`, at the level of sections over an
   192	open `U`: the canonical ring homomorphism `k →+* Γ(X, U)`. -/
   193	noncomputable def Scheme.overAlgebraMap (U : X.Opens) : k →+* Γ(X, U) :=
   194	  ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ (X ↘ Spec (.of k)).appTop ≫
   195	    X.presheaf.map (homOfLE le_top).op).hom
   196	
   197	lemma Scheme.overAlgebraMap_naturality {U V : X.Opensᵒᵖ} (i : U ⟶ V) :
   198	    ((X.presheaf.map i).hom).comp (X.overAlgebraMap k U.unop) =
   199	      X.overAlgebraMap k V.unop := by
   200	  rw [Scheme.overAlgebraMap, Scheme.overAlgebraMap, ← CommRingCat.hom_comp]
   201	  congr 1
   202	  simp only [Category.assoc, ← X.presheaf.map_comp]
   203	  congr 1
   204	
   205	lemma Scheme.overAlgebraMap_apply_res {U V : X.Opensᵒᵖ} (i : U ⟶ V) (r : k) :
   206	    (X.presheaf.map i).hom (X.overAlgebraMap k U.unop r) =
   207	      X.overAlgebraMap k V.unop r :=
   208	  DFunLike.congr_fun (X.overAlgebraMap_naturality k i) r
   209	
   210	/-- The `k`-module structure on `Γ(X, U)` for a scheme over `Spec k`, by restriction of
   211	scalars along `Scheme.overAlgebraMap`. Deliberately *not* a global instance: it would
   212	overlap with mathlib's `Algebra R Γ(Spec R, U)` instance through the tautological
   213	`OverClass X X`. Activate it with `attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule` or `letI`
   214	where needed. -/
   215	@[reducible] noncomputable def Scheme.overModule (U : X.Opens) : Module k Γ(X, U) :=
   216	  (X.overAlgebraMap k U).toModule
   217	
   218	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule
   219	
   220	lemma Scheme.overModule_smul_def {U : X.Opens} (r : k) (s : Γ(X, U)) :
   221	    r • s = X.overAlgebraMap k U r * s := rfl
   222	
   223	/-- The structure sheaf of a scheme `X` over `Spec k`, as a presheaf of `k`-modules on
   224	`Opens X`: sections are `Γ(X, U)` with the `k`-action of `Scheme.overModule`, restriction
   225	maps are those of the structure sheaf. -/
   226	noncomputable def Scheme.moduleKPresheaf : X.Opensᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat.{u} k where
   227	  obj U := ModuleCat.of k Γ(X, U.unop)
   228	  map {U V} i := ModuleCat.ofHom
   229	    { toFun := (X.presheaf.map i).hom
   230	      map_add' := map_add _
   231	      map_smul' := fun r s ↦ by
   232	        simp only [Scheme.overModule_smul_def, map_mul, RingHom.id_apply,
   233	          X.overAlgebraMap_apply_res k i r] }
   234	  map_id U := by
   235	    ext s
   236	    exact DFunLike.congr_fun (congrArg CommRingCat.Hom.hom (X.presheaf.map_id U)) s
   237	  map_comp {U V W} i j := by
   238	    ext s
   239	    exact DFunLike.congr_fun (congrArg CommRingCat.Hom.hom (X.presheaf.map_comp i j)) s
   240	
   241	/-- The underlying types-valued presheaf of `Scheme.moduleKPresheaf` is that of the
   242	structure sheaf. -/
   243	noncomputable def Scheme.moduleKPresheafCompForgetIso :
   244	    X.moduleKPresheaf k ⋙ CategoryTheory.forget (ModuleCat.{u} k) ≅
   245	      X.presheaf ⋙ CategoryTheory.forget CommRingCat :=
   246	  NatIso.ofComponents (fun _ ↦ Iso.refl _) (fun _ ↦ rfl)
   247	
   248	lemma Scheme.isSheaf_moduleKPresheaf :
   249	    Presheaf.IsSheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology (X : TopCat)) (X.moduleKPresheaf k) := by
   250	  have h : TopCat.Presheaf.IsSheaf (C := ModuleCat.{u} k) (X := (X : TopCat))
   251	      (X.moduleKPresheaf k) := by
   252	    rw [TopCat.Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_comp' (CategoryTheory.forget (ModuleCat.{u} k))
   253	      (X.moduleKPresheaf k)]
   254	    change Presheaf.IsSheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology (X : TopCat)) _
   255	    rw [Presheaf.isSheaf_of_iso_iff (X.moduleKPresheafCompForgetIso k)]
   256	    exact (TopCat.Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_comp'
   257	      (CategoryTheory.forget CommRingCat) X.presheaf).mp X.toSheafedSpace.IsSheaf
   258	  exact h
   259	
   260	/-- The structure sheaf of a scheme `X` over `Spec k`, as a sheaf of `k`-modules on the
   261	small Zariski site of `X`. Its sections over `U` are *definitionally*
   262	`ModuleCat.of k Γ(X, U)` (with the `Scheme.overModule` action) and its restriction maps
   263	are definitionally those of the structure sheaf; see `Scheme.moduleKSheaf_obj` and
   264	`Scheme.moduleKSheaf_map_apply`. -/
   265	noncomputable def Scheme.moduleKSheaf :
   266	    Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology (X : TopCat)) (ModuleCat.{u} k) :=
   267	  ⟨X.moduleKPresheaf k, X.isSheaf_moduleKPresheaf k⟩
   268	
   269	@[simp]
   270	lemma Scheme.moduleKSheaf_obj (U : X.Opens) :
   271	    (X.moduleKSheaf k).obj.obj (op U) = ModuleCat.of k Γ(X, U) := rfl
   272	
   273	lemma Scheme.moduleKSheaf_map_apply {U V : X.Opensᵒᵖ} (i : U ⟶ V)
   274	    (s : Γ(X, U.unop)) :
   275	    ((X.moduleKSheaf k).obj.map i).hom s = (X.presheaf.map i).hom s := rfl
   276	
   277	/-- `H⁰` of the structure sheaf of `X` over `Spec k` is the module of global sections
   278	`Γ(X, ⊤)`, `k`-linearly (with the `Scheme.overModule` structure on the right). -/
   279	noncomputable def Scheme.moduleKSheafHZero :
   280	    Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf k) 0 ≃ₗ[k] Γ(X, ⊤) :=

   282	    (isTerminalTop : IsTerminal (⊤ : X.Opens))
   283	    (X.moduleKSheaf k)
   284

     9	/-!
    10	# Sheaves of `k`-modules: finite-length carriers
    11	
    12	For a scheme `C` over `Spec k` this file develops the finite-length side of `ModuleCat k`-valued
    13	sheaf cohomology: the cohomology carriers `HModule` (global) and `HModule'` (evaluated at an open),
    14	their degree-zero `k`-linear identifications with Hom groups, the two finiteness hypotheses
    15	`IsAffineHModuleVanishing` (vanishing of `Hⁱ` on affine opens for `i > 0`) and `IsHModuleHomFinite`
    16	(finiteness over `k` of the global sections), and the Čech-side carriers. The structure sheaf these
    17	act on is constructed in `Presheaf.lean` and `SheafProperty.lean`.
    18	
    19	On a proper integral `Spec k`-scheme `IsHModuleHomFinite` holds for the structure sheaf, the
    20	geometric input being finiteness of `Γ(C, O_C)` over `k`. No such instance is available for
    21	`IsAffineHModuleVanishing`: producing one requires the comparison between Čech and derived-functor
    22	cohomology on an acyclic cover, which is not proved here.
    23	
    24	## Main results
    25	
    26	* `HModule`, `HModule'`: `ModuleCat k`-valued sheaf cohomology, globally and at an open.
    27	* `HModule_zero_linearEquiv`, `HModule'_zero_linearEquiv`: the degree-zero identification with a
    28	  `k`-linear Hom group.
    29	* `IsAffineHModuleVanishing`, `IsHModuleHomFinite`: the two finiteness hypotheses.
    30	* `module_finite_globalSections_of_isProper`: `Γ(C, O_C)` is finite over `k` when `C` is integral
    31	  and proper over `Spec k`.
    32	* `instIsHModuleHomFinite_toModuleKSheaf`: the resulting instance for the structure sheaf.
    33	* `Scheme.cechCochain`, `Scheme.cechCohomology`: Čech cochains and cohomology of a sheaf of
    34	  `k`-modules with respect to an indexed family of opens.
    35	-/
    36	
    37	set_option autoImplicit false
    38	
    39	universe u v
    40	
    41	open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace AlgebraicGeometry
    42	
    43	namespace AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme
    44	
    45	/-- Sheaf cohomology for `ModuleCat k`-valued sheaves, the analogue of `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.H`.
    46	Mathlib's `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.H` is parameterised over `Sheaf J AddCommGrpCat` only, which loses
    47	the `k`-linear structure needed to define a genus. The result here carries `Module k` automatically
    48	via `CategoryTheory.Abelian.Ext.instModule`, so `Module.finrank k` is well-defined on it. It is an
    49	`abbrev` rather than a `def` so that instance synthesis sees through the wrapper to find the
    50	`Module k` and `AddCommGroup` instances. -/
    51	noncomputable abbrev HModule
    52	    (k : Type u) [Field k]
    53	    {C : Type v} [Category.{u, v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
    54	    [HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u} k)] [HasExt (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k))]
    55	    (F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k)) (n : ℕ) : Type (u+1) :=
    56	  Abelian.Ext ((constantSheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k)).obj (ModuleCat.of k k)) F n
